articles.title: Bitcoin hovers near $80,000 and Ethereum at $2,370 as macro uncertainty and weak institutional flows weigh on crypto markets
articles.content: In recent developments, Bitcoin has dropped to roughly $80,685, while Ethereum hovers around $2,370 due to various market influences. Major altcoins such as XRP and Dogecoin have also experienced dips, some decreasing by 2.2%. A noticeable decline in institutional interest is evident, with substantial outflows from Bitcoin and Ether ETFs. Both Bitcoin and Ethereum are facing challenges sustaining their momentum amidst the market's volatility.

articles.title: Lenskart, Meesho among top picks as value retail leads India's consumption story: Siddhartha Khemka
articles.content: Value-focused retail formats are growing, while premium categories experience challenges due to stock availability issues. Recent demand fluctuated with a dip noted in September and October, with expectations for improvement in mid-October. Beauty products significantly influence sales, contributing to the overall trends in the market. Rural incomes may pose risks to discretionary spending as festive season approaches. Companies with effective inventory management and store-level traction are better positioned for growth.

articles.title: Sebi orders Avadhut Sathe, academy to refund Rs 546 crore
articles.content: The Securities and Exchange Board of India has directed Avadhut Sathe Trading Academy to refund ₹546.18 crore to investors. Avadhut Sathe and his academy provided unregistered investment advisory services under the pretext of education. The regulator found that misleading testimonials were circulated while concealing overall trading losses. A penalty of ₹11.5 crore was imposed on Sathe and the academy for their actions.

articles.title: Anthropic IPO: What should investors consider when valuing the AI company? Aswath Damodaran explains
articles.content: Anthropic is on track for an IPO expected in mid-November, reporting impressive revenues of $16.3 billion. However, the company faces a staggering net loss of over $80 billion for the year. Valuation expert Aswath Damodaran warns that IPO investor metrics can be erratic and heavily influenced by market sentiment. As Anthropic navigates an evolving business model, investors are advised to look beyond venture capital evaluations for a clearer understanding.

articles.title: Growth, value stocks set for reshuffle as S&P adopts new rules
articles.content: S&P Dow Jones Indices will soon change its rules for classifying growth and value shares. The new criteria will incorporate intangible assets, forward earnings, and free cash flow instead of relying on 12-month price momentum. These changes are expected to affect approximately $375 billion of passive funds linked to the index. FTSE Russell is also considering adjustments due to the dominance of technology companies.

articles.title: BPCL reports 21.45% drop in Q2 FY27 net profit, attributes losses to fuel pricing issues
articles.content: Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL) has reported a 21.45% decline in consolidated net profit for Q2 FY27. The decline is attributed to losses from the sale of petrol, diesel, and LPG, which affected marketing margins. Consolidated revenue from operations increased by 29.7% compared to the previous fiscal year. As of September 30, 2026, BPCL's cumulative under recoveries on LPG reached ₹17,334.40 crore.

articles.title: Adani Power profit surges 142% on strong demand amid weak rains
articles.content: Adani Power has reported a 142% increase in net profit for the July-September quarter. This profit was driven by strong electricity demand and exceptional prior-period income. Operating revenue for the company saw a nearly 30% increase compared to the previous year. The company also recognized significant revenue due to adjustments in historic energy charges under its power purchase agreements.

articles.title: US consumer sentiment near record low ahead of midterm elections
articles.content: In October, consumer sentiment in the U.S. plummeted to a concerning 48.0, driven by rising prices and economic worries amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Survey results suggest that independents show the steepest drop in confidence, approaching historical lows. Additionally, inflation expectations have risen, marking a continuation of trends from earlier this year. Federal Reserve officials are attentively observing these shifts as they plan future interest rate adjustments.

After disappointing earnings from firms such as Meta and Lam Research, mixed sentiment looms over the market, especially with the midterm elections on the horizon.

articles.title: Indians remit $2.7 billion overseas in August, led by travel
articles.content: Outward remittances under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS) stood at $2.7 billion, with travel accounting for the largest chunk. Indians spent $1.6 billion on travel in August, from $1.7 billion in July, while $275 million were spent on maintenan-ce of relatives. Indian citizen spent $321 million on investments in equity and debt, while $191 million on studies abroad.

articles.title: Gross FDI inflows to India fall to $11 billion in August
articles.content: Gross foreign direct investment (FDI) to India decreased to $11 billion in August, from $14 billion a month ago. Net FDI to India slows $3 billion in August, from $7 billion in July. Financial services, communication services, computer services and manufacturing accounted for around 73% of total FDI equity inflows during April-August 2026.

articles.title: Swiggy sinks 16% to record low as quick-commerce losses widen
articles.content: Shares of Swiggy fell by 16.4% to ₹176.70, marking a record low for the company. This decline raises concerns over cash burn and achieving profitability in its quick-commerce business. Analysts are questioning Swiggy's strategic choices and execution following its market debut. The widening losses in the quick-commerce segment have drawn attention to the company's overall performance.
